name: RS274/NGC (reference)
description: Generic RS274/NGC as defined by NIST IR 6556. The test reference: every code it writes is in that standard. Our own post, not a controller vendor's. Holes use G81, G82 and G83 as NIST defines them (G98 returns to the height at the start of each line; G83 rapids out to that clear height between pecks). G73 is not in the standard, so chip-break holes are written as plain moves. NIST leaves G83's re-entry clearance to the control: the 0.5 mm here only draws and simulates the pecks. Tapped holes use G84 as NIST defines it: the spindle already turning clockwise, feed in, reverse, feed out, the feed the pitch times the speed.
